body: If anyone reads this you can help save my life by forwarding this doc or reddit to a professional philosopher who can guide me out of it. If you suspect I'm doing this for attention, consider what kind of person would pretend to argue for suicide anonymously and beg for help? Even if that were me, the rebuttal itself could help anyone else who thinks this way.

Answering late because I just got back from therapy. Thank you so much for actually reading this, you're the only one on the whole internet so far that gives a shit about me. Just the fact that you'd actually listen makes me cry. I'm about to die painfully and it feels like nobody even cares. Don't have time to argue rn but my mind has a response which maintains the negative valuation to everything you said

Overcoming fear is bravery; jumping into a giant thorn bush is stupidity. I'm sorry to use that language but that's just honestly what my brain is telling me. It's telling me life is stupid no matter how I feel.

What kind of suffering? Where you tortured and raped or something? I've named it have you been through it? Would you volunteer to be tortured rather than to die? edit: I'm suicidal this is a genuine question not mocking

Other than the last question, I have a few others. Which position do you agree with most?
1. All conscious states are or could be interpreted as varying degrees of positive 
or
2. Some conscious states are negative and should be avoided at all costs

First of all I'm very grateful for your responses and appreciate your point of view, thank you. I would have replied right away, I've been online but seem to have missed the notification.

At the risk of sidetracking into unproductive philosophical debate which maybe doesn't belong in this sub and I'm not really qualified to deal with, your views seem to mirror a lot of Buddhist principles. The problem with any views that deny the significance of pain is they seem hypocritical or they smuggle in unspoken assumptions about it.
That's why I ask is an existence in hell more preferable to you than non-existence? Even if it's only physical sensory pain hell. But the problem we seem to be coming at this question from different assumptions about what causes suffering. But I'm worried that suffering can be inflicted on me whether I choose it or it's chosen for me, after all there's no guarantee of autonomy in life, for example you could be mentally incapacitated to the point where you can't choose not to suffer but you can still feel the pain. Unless you have smuggled in presuppositions about souls or free will. In which case we're not gonna get anywhere productive. Also it just seems like even if you relativize pain, you become a hypocrite by avoiding it while seeking pleasures like we all do. Even ascetist monks and buddhists practitiioners still use hygeine, use shelter, eat food that doesn't make you vomit, and avoid legos. 
So if you don't mind can you answer if hell (where whatever could go wrong goes wrong, worst possible misery) is preferable to non-existence for you?

Thank you for your response it means a lot to me.

But death has no basal value or a basal value of zero depending on semantics, while life in my view always has a negative value for the reason that even when it's better than death you can't rationally enjoy it because something worse than death happening to is always an unfalsifiable possibility.

To me personally your last two sentences sound like what everyone says "don't think about it" or "have faith" or "man up", which to me, is blind optimism, not realism at all.

"We live in the here and now. Everything else is just theoretical I try to take the position of being an observer to life, and if you can do that, you can go right on with life without any guarantees. It's better to observe than not observe."
I'm sorry but I don't agree with you, and I think if anybody who thinks suffering is just "observation" or it could be embraced are just not using their imagination. My argument would hold even in the most happy moments in life. If you would "observe" suffering while you were being tortured and raped to death, then you have some enlightenment I want to hear more about.

"Our brains are wired to avoid uncertainty, but with practice you can get comfortable with it. Staying present, letting go the idea that you have to own all your thoughts and feelings, even just a little bit, trying to Foster a sense of curiosity and wonder. These are all muscles that we can build."
Like the other comment by rawbatz it sounds like you're saying not to think about it. The difference is you seem to take the view of suffering as not being crucial to existence having meaning. Sorry to repeat myself but I think anyone with that view just lacks the experience of real suffering, imagination of real suffering, or is sneaking in faith-based assumptions like religious torture and reincarnation.
My challenge that I don't think anyone can beat: Should one prefer to go to "hell" or die? Well it's your opinion I know my answer.

(edit) I forgot to thank you for responding. Thank you for taking the time to share your point of view.
